exercise.name: Landmine Kneeling One Arm Shoulder Press

reference.title: Landmine Kneeling One Arm Shoulder Press
reference.listing: Animated GIF (title from the catalog listing; the page could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace at the shoulder, breathe out as you press, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.4 s up, short pause, about 2 s down

prescription.load: User-chosen; pick a load you can press for the target reps with 1-3 reps in reserve (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)

cues.text: Kneel tall facing the landmine, knees hip width on a pad, toes tucked; hold the end of the bar in front of your right shoulder, left hand on the hip, glutes and abs tight.
Breathe out and press the bar up and forward along its arc until the arm is long.
Reach a little at the top without shrugging; hips and ribs stay stacked.
Breathe in and lower the bar back to the front of the shoulder under control.
Re-brace, stay tall; repeat, then switch sides.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back or arching the low back to push the bar
mistakes.fix: Squeeze the glutes and keep the ribs down; lighten the load.

mistakes.mistake: Twisting the trunk toward the pressing arm
mistakes.fix: Keep the shoulders and hips square to the pivot.

mistakes.mistake: Shrugging the shoulder to the ear at the top
mistakes.fix: Reach forward and up, shoulder away from the ear.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the bar drop onto the shoulder
mistakes.fix: Lower over about 2 s and stop at the front of the shoulder.

kinematics.norm: Tall-kneeling: both knees under the hips about hip-width apart, thighs about vertical, toes tucked (clinical opinion)
The bar's arc takes the hand up and forward rather than straight overhead: the upper arm finishes in front of the head, short of full overhead elevation (clinical opinion)
About 90 degrees or more at the bottom with the hand at the shoulder, nearly straight at the top (clinical opinion)
The bar rises from about 30 degrees above the floor at the shoulder; the hand moves on the arc set by the bar length (geometry)
Controlled, about 1.5 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)
Trunk stays tall; a unilateral load raises oblique and back-stabilizer activity to resist side bending (Saeterbakken 2012; Trunk 2005)

sources.title: GymVisual #8849, Landmine Kneeling One Arm Shoulder Press, animated GIF (movement reference; page not readable here)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2012, muscle activity of the core during bilateral, unilateral, seated and standing resistance exercise (Eur J Appl Physiol 112:1671-1678)
Trunk muscle electromyographic activity with unstable and unilateral exercises (J Strength Cond Res 19(1):193-201, 2005; PubMed 15705034)

cautions: Shoulder pain: shorten the range or lighten the load; stop if pain is sharp (clinical opinion).
Seat the bar end fully in the pivot and keep the area around the bar clear.
Knee discomfort: use a thicker pad.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Half-kneeling (one knee up) for a wider base.

muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Main mover: the press goes up and forward along the bar's arc, so the front of the shoulder does most of the work (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Helps lift the arm; less than in a vertical press because the arm stays in front of the body (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straightens the elbow in the top half.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Upward rotation and elevation of the shoulder blade overhead.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Upward rotation of the shoulder blade so the arm can reach overhead.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Stop the trunk side-bending away from the one-sided load. A unilateral press gave much higher external oblique activity than a bilateral press (Saeterbakken 2012).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Stop the trunk side-bending away from the one-sided load. A unilateral press gave much higher external oblique activity than a bilateral press (Saeterbakken 2012).
muscleNotes.core: Braces the trunk; kneeling takes away help from the legs, so the trunk works more (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Both glutes squeeze to keep the hips extended and the pelvis stacked over the knees (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Both glutes squeeze to keep the hips extended and the pelvis stacked over the knees (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the trunk tall; a unilateral press activated the back stabilizers more than a bilateral press (Trunk 2005; Saeterbakken 2012).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the trunk tall; a unilateral press activated the back stabilizers more than a bilateral press (Trunk 2005; Saeterbakken 2012).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: centres the ball of the shoulder as the arm rises.

guides.label: Hand rides up the bar's arc
